note: Peekaboo: records located or identified despite an incorrect label, description or location, or an assurance that they were not there. Facts and dates only; each record names who found the mismatch and what the item is. Read by the Peekaboo webapp (/peekaboo/, branch section/peekaboo) through its sync script, by the tag peekaboo.

records.title: Internet Archive copy of Newman, Glamorgan (1995): the catalogue description is a children's story blurb
records.place_text: Catalogue data of a published book (Glamorgan; entries for Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Leckwith and Cogan)
records.description: The Internet Archive lending copy of John Newman's Glamorgan (The Buildings of Wales, 1995; identifier glamorganmidglam0000newm) carries, as its description, the summary of a children's picture book: “A very hairy but not-too-scary monster story. One dark, stormy night, Owl, Mouse and Rabbit are afraid. Could it be the Monster of the Woods knocking at the door? This warm, funny tale about friendship has a wonderfully unexpected twist.” The book itself is a 717-page architectural guide. The same text is the summary note (MARC field 520) in the catalogue record attached to the copy, which is a copy of OCLC WorldCat record 33858574 last changed on 8 June 2022. That record's title statement also reads “by Stephen Hughes and Anthony Ward”, while its creator field names John Newman. A reader searching the description would not find the book; the book holds the Llandough, Leckwith and Cogan entries catalogued as AR-NEWMAN-1995.

detail.heading: What the catalogue shows
detail.text: Description: a children's story about Owl, Mouse and Rabbit and “the Monster of the Woods”. Physical description: 717 pages, 64 unnumbered pages of plates. Subjects: architecture and historic buildings of Glamorgan.

detail.heading: What the item is
detail.text: John Newman, Glamorgan (Mid Glamorgan, South Glamorgan and West Glamorgan), The Buildings of Wales, Penguin Books and University of Wales Press, 1995; scanned by the Internet Archive on 9 June 2022; controlled lending only.

detail.heading: Where the text sits
detail.text: MARC 520 (summary) in the item's MARC file, mirrored into the description field. MARC 001 ocm33858574 (OCoLC); MARC 005 20220608130827. The title statement (MARC 245) names Stephen Hughes and Anthony Ward and not the author.

detail.heading: Correction requested
detail.text: Remove the children's story summary from this record and give the author in the title statement. Draft notices to the Internet Archive and to OCLC WorldCat are listed in Peekaboo; nothing has been sent.

records.title: Glamorgan Archives DBDT/79/1: catalogue description corrected after the original was examined (14 September 2026)
records.place_text: Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff (the lease's own property); not Llandough
records.description: On 26 August 2026 Glamorgan Archives was asked to examine the original of DBDT/79/1, catalogued as a counterpart lease of land in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff “from the Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams, May 1877”, and to report its physical contents separately from the catalogue description. The archive's reply of 14 September 2026 (ref. 2026/3893) reads: “The catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 had a few small errors which have now been corrected.” The original is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport, for a plot in Pembroke Terrace in the parish of St John the Baptist, Cardiff. The archive found no mention of Llandough, Great House Farm or Tŷ Mawr, or of any property outside Pembroke Terrace. The catalogue wording was wrong and was put right on inspection; the deed itself concerns Cardiff property (KF-02).

provenance.obtained: Reply received 14 September 2026 to an enquiry of 26 August 2026.

scope.label: Peekaboo: catalogue corrected after inspection (deed is Cardiff property)
scope.reason: The catalogue description did not match the original; the original concerns Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff.

detail.heading: Catalogue wording before
detail.text: “Lease (counterpart) of land and premises situate in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff, from the Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams, May 1877 [1 parchment, plan in margin].”

detail.heading: The original, as examined
detail.text: Counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877; grantors the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute; lessee Mr John Williams of Newport; a plot in Pembroke Terrace, parish of St John the Baptist, Cardiff; marginal plan shows a property on Pembroke Terrace.

detail.heading: Found by
detail.text: The holder, on a physical check of the original requested on 26 August 2026.

detail.heading: What it does and does not establish
detail.text: It shows a catalogue description that did not match the original and was corrected. It does not place the lease at Llandough; the archive found no Llandough reference in it.

changes.note: Observation added: catalogue correction confirmed by the holder after inspection.
